methodology: Read-only transfer audit. Archetypes were selected from public two-month Standard and Pioneer metagame aggregations. Each selected archetype has at least 100 source-reported decklists in the selection set and at least 100 ranked decks in the corresponding card-presence fingerprint. Scores are explicit priors for Thun-format research, not predicted win rates and not authorization to replace a Champion deck.

principles: Successful decks usually make a relevant play by turn two.
Role compression is disproportionately valuable: one card often advances multiple strategic functions.
The best synergy enablers retain baseline utility when the ideal payoff is absent.
Core functions require redundant card names, especially under the Thun three-copy limit.
The mana base is part of the strategy through fixing, utility, flood protection or land triggers.
Top decks retain reload, resilience or a second wave after the first exchange.
Interaction must be available at the correct turn and speed, not merely present in aggregate.
A payoff must materially convert setup into damage, cards, mana, board control or inevitability.
Strong decks have useful mana sinks or card selection to reduce late-game dead draws.
Transferability is constrained by the least replaceable core function, not by the percentage of replaceable cards.

archetypes.name: Standard Izzet Prowess
fingerprint: Low threat count backed by a very high density of one- and two-mana noncreature spells
Cantrips are simultaneously consistency, trigger density and damage conversion
Tempo interaction protects the clock while preserving multi-spell turns
Evasion and burst damage punish opponents who tap out
functional_replacements: Rare burst threats can be replaced by a wider package of uncommon prowess or magecraft threats
Rare modal interaction can be split across separate burn, bounce and counterspell slots
non_reproducible_functions: The best rare threats combine burst, evasion and resilience in one card
Rare dual and utility lands preserve both speed and late-game value

archetypes.name: Standard Izzet Spellementals
fingerprint: Approximately twelve spell-cost-reduction or spell-scaling creatures
Large instant and sorcery density with cantrips, burn and counters
Threats become efficient through graveyard or spell-count conditions
The deck can switch between tempo and a longer permission game
functional_replacements: Rare top-end spell creatures can be replaced by delve, cost-reduction or graveyard-scaling uncommons
Rare flexible interaction can be divided into narrower but efficient answers
non_reproducible_functions: Rare threats provide unusually high power while leaving mana open
Premium dual lands reduce the cost of playing reactive two-color Magic

archetypes.name: Four-Color Control
fingerprint: Best-in-class interaction and card advantage are selected across four colors
A rare-heavy mana base enables early interaction despite broad color requirements
Sweepers and card draw exchange resources before a compact finisher package takes over
Utility lands and modal cards reduce dead draws
functional_replacements: Individual rare answers can be replaced by narrower common or uncommon answers
Planeswalker finishers can be approximated by resilient creatures or repeatable enchantments
non_reproducible_functions: A common/uncommon four-color mana base cannot preserve the same early castability
Rare modal cards compress fixing, interaction and card advantage
The deck loses too many virtual spell slots when its lands provide only mana

archetypes.name: Mono-Green Landfall
fingerprint: Turn-one acceleration followed by landfall or land-scaling threats
Sacrifice and fetch lands create multiple triggers from normal land drops
Payoffs turn future lands into board development rather than dead draws
Mono-color construction protects castability
functional_replacements: Rare fetch lands can be approximated by slower common sacrifice lands
Rare role-compression creatures can be replaced by separate ramp and payoff cards
non_reproducible_functions: Badgermole Cub-level cards combine acceleration and threat quality at rare efficiency
The strongest rare payoffs recover more effectively from removal

archetypes.name: Jeskai Lessons
fingerprint: A named spell engine is played in near-complete four-of packages
Tablet and repeated Lessons convert cheap spells into cumulative advantage
Three colors supply removal, counters and finishers
The deck is consistent because the engine pieces reinforce one another
functional_replacements: The broad spellslinger shell can be rebuilt with magecraft, flashback or cost-reduction packages
Some rare interaction can be replaced by narrower answers
non_reproducible_functions: Replacing the named Tablet/Lesson engine changes the archetype rather than preserving it
Three-color early interaction is much less reliable with low-rarity lands
The three-copy limit weakens a tightly coupled four-of engine

archetypes.name: Selesnya Gearhulk
fingerprint: Turn-one mana creature into high-quality three- and four-mana plays
Creature toolbox and protection reduce the cost of situational cards
Counters and go-wide pressure produce a fast clock
Rare creatures compress tutor, body, protection and payoff functions
functional_replacements: The shell can become Selesnya counters or creature midrange
Toolbox effects can be approximated by redundant functional packages
non_reproducible_functions: Brightglass Gearhulk-level tutor plus body role compression is unavailable
Rare threats preserve pressure and card quality after removal

archetypes.name: Pioneer Izzet Prowess
fingerprint: Eight or more one-mana spell-matter threats
Cheap burn, pump and cantrips enable multi-spell turns
Interaction doubles as damage or tempo
Redundant threat and spell classes preserve consistency
direct_functions: Monastery Swiftspear and other low-rarity prowess creatures
functional_replacements: Rare threats can be spread across more common and uncommon spell-matter creatures
Premium modal cards can be replaced by narrower effects
non_reproducible_functions: Rare dual lands and utility lands preserve both speed and reach
The best rare threats provide more resilience than low-rarity substitutes

archetypes.name: Pioneer Red Deck Wins
fingerprint: High density of one-mana creatures and damage spells
Nearly every nonland card advances the damage race
Pump and burn convert small creatures into large tempo swings
Mono-red construction and redundant card classes support the three-copy limit
functional_replacements: Rare threats can be replaced by additional haste, prowess or burn cards
Rare land-based reach can be partially replaced by spell density
non_reproducible_functions: The best rare threats combine immediate damage, resilience and anti-lifegain
Utility lands reduce flood without consuming spell slots

archetypes.name: Pioneer Golgari Midrange
fingerprint: Turn-one discard or removal followed by efficient standalone threats
Flexible answers cover creatures, permanents and graveyards
Threats generate value or remain relevant after a one-for-one exchange
Utility lands add pressure and reduce flood
functional_replacements: Rare threats can be replaced by ETB creatures, Adventures and recursion
Rare universal answers can be approximated by a diversified answer suite
non_reproducible_functions: Rare threats provide unusually high standalone rate and role compression
Rare lands contribute material pressure without reducing interaction count

archetypes.name: Pioneer Dimir Ninjas
fingerprint: Evasive one-mana creatures enable combat-damage and ninjutsu payoffs
Cheap discard and removal protect the connection window
Successful attacks convert tempo into card advantage
The deck can pivot into a disruptive midrange plan
direct_functions: Moon-Circuit Hacker and other Ninja payoffs
functional_replacements: Rare Kaito and Sheoldred backup can be replaced by slower draw engines or resilient uncommons
Premium discard can be approximated by conditional discard
non_reproducible_functions: Rare backup threats stabilize games where combat connection fails
Premium lands preserve early interaction and creature deployment simultaneously

archetypes.name: Pioneer Azorius Control
fingerprint: Early counters and exile removal trade efficiently
Sweepers reset creature-heavy boards
Card draw and planeswalkers create inevitability
Utility lands provide win conditions and flood protection
functional_replacements: Planeswalkers can be approximated by repeatable enchantments and resilient finishers
Rare removal can be replaced by narrower answers
non_reproducible_functions: Premium uncounterable sweepers are rare
Planeswalkers compress card advantage, defense and win condition
Rare dual and utility lands support interaction without sacrificing inevitability

archetypes.name: Abzan Greasefang
fingerprint: Place a specific large Vehicle in the graveyard
Resolve Greasefang and immediately return the Vehicle with haste
Use discard, selection and removal to protect a compact combo
Retain a midrange backup plan through standalone Vehicles and creatures
functional_replacements: The broad graveyard-Vehicle theme could become a different reanimator or artifact deck
non_reproducible_functions: Greasefang and Parhelion II are rare named combo pieces
No low-rarity replacement preserves immediate temporary reanimation, haste and the same attack output
Replacing the combo changes the archetype rather than translating it
